title: Find the Length of the Longest Common Prefix
statement:
You get two arrays of positive integers, `arr1` and `arr2`. A prefix of a positive integer is the number formed by its first one or more decimal digits (so `12` is a prefix of `1205`, but `20` is not). Two integers share a common prefix `c` when `c` is a prefix of each of them.

Over every pair `(x, y)` with `x` taken from `arr1` and `y` taken from `arr2`, find the longest common prefix and return its number of digits. Pairs inside the same array do not count. If no pair has any common prefix, return `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every pair `(x, y)` digit by digit is O(n₁ · n₂ · d), far too slow for 5 · 10^4 numbers on each side. But any common prefix of `x` and `y` is simply a prefix of `y` that also happens to be a prefix of some number in `arr1`. A number has at most 9 prefixes, and dropping the last digit (`Math.floor(value / 10)`) walks through all of them. So we store every prefix of every number in `arr1` in a set, then for each number in `arr2` look for its longest prefix in that set.

## Approach

1. For each `num` in `arr1`, add `num` and every number obtained by repeatedly removing its last digit to `prefixes`.
2. For each `num` in `arr2`, start with `value = num` and remove last digits until `value` is in `prefixes` or reaches `0`.
3. The first `value` found is the longest prefix of `num` shared with `arr1`; if it is positive, update `best` with its digit count.
4. Return `best` (`0` if no number ever matched).

## Example 1, step by step

`arr1 = [1, 10, 100]` gives `prefixes = {1, 10, 100}`. For `1000` in `arr2`, `1000` is not in the set, so it shrinks to `100`, which is. `100` has 3 digits, so `best = 3` and the answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((n₁ + n₂) · d) with d ≤ 9 digits: every number walks through its prefixes once.
- Space: O(n₁ · d) for the set of prefixes.

## Pitfalls

- Matching numbers within the same array is not allowed; only `arr1` builds the set and only `arr2` queries it.
- Return the number of digits of the shared prefix, not the prefix itself.
- Stop as soon as a prefix is found: shrinking further only gives shorter answers.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prefixes` | every prefix of every number in `arr1` |
| `num` | the number being processed |
| `value` | the current prefix of `num` |
| `best` | longest shared prefix length found so far |

narration.2: This set will hold every prefix of every number in arr1.
narration.3: Take each number of the first array.
narration.4: Start from the whole number, its longest prefix.
narration.5: Keep going until all digits are removed.
narration.7: Drop the last digit to get the next shorter prefix.
narration.11: No common prefix has been found yet.
narration.12: Now take each number of the second array.
narration.14: Shrink it until it becomes a prefix that arr1 also has, or nothing is left.
narration.15: Drop the last digit and try the shorter prefix.
narration.17: A shared prefix was found; it is the longest one for this number.
narration.18: Keep the largest digit count seen so far.
narration.21: Return the longest common prefix length over all pairs.
